├── ja/                     # 日本語版 Web 形式リファレンス (general-01 ~ 11)
└── en/                     # English Web Reference (general-01 ~ 11)
```

---

## 📊 Feature Comparison Matrix & Real-world Benchmarks

**Last Updated: 2026-10-12**

A side-by-side comparison of advanced features (formula engine, PivotTables, charts, password encryption) and measured performance between popular open-source libraries and **osbxl**.

### 1. Feature Support Matrix

| Feature | osbxl (5 Languages) | Apache POI (Java) | openpyxl (Python) | PhpSpreadsheet (PHP) | ExcelJS / SheetJS (JS) |
|---|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|
| **.xlsx Read & Write** | **◎ Fast & Stable** | **◎** | **◎** | **◎** | **◎** |
| **Headless Formula Calculation** (Evaluating values without Excel) | **◎ ~500 Functions** (XLOOKUP, VLOOKUP, etc.) | **◯ 300–400 Functions** (Evaluator) | **✕ Not Supported** (None until Excel opens) | **△ Partial** (Heavy & limited) | **✕ Not Supported** (Requires paid SheetJS Pro) |
| **Tables & Structured References** (e.g. `SUM(Table[Column])`) | **◎ Full Native Eval** | **△ No Calculation** (Save only) | **✕ Cannot Eval** | **✕ Cannot Eval** | **✕ Cannot Eval** |
| **AutoFilter** | **◎ Advanced Filter** | **◯** | **◯** | **◯** | **◯** |
| **PivotTable Creation** | **◎ Standard API** | **◯ Low-level XML** | **△ Read-focused** | **✕ Not Supported** | **✕ Not Supported** |
| **Chart & Graph Generation** | **◎ 2D & 3D Charts** | **◯ Via XDDF** | **◯ 2D/3D Support** | **△ Limited rendering** | **✕–△ Minimal** |
| **Password Encryption / Decryption** | **◎ Built-in** | **◯ Standard** | **✕ Needs 3rd-party tool** | **✕ Needs extension** | **✕ Not Supported** |
| **Cell Comments (Notes & Threads)** | **◎ Both Notes & Threads** | **◯ Notes only** | **◯ Comments only** | **◯ Comments only** | **◯ Comments only** |
| **AI Codegen Optimization** | **◎ Official AI Skill** (Zero hallucination) | **✕ Unofficial** (Frequent fake APIs) | **✕ Unofficial** | **✕ Unofficial** | **✕ Unofficial** |

### 2. Standard 200-Row (800-Cell) Benchmark

Measured under the same development environment (Linux x86_64) generating a standard business report (**200 rows × 4 columns = 800 cells + SUM formula**).

| Language | Library | Time (sec) | Memory (MB) | Highlights |
|---|---|:---:|:---:|---|
| **Java** (JDK 1.8) | Apache POI 5.2.5 (XSSF) **osbxl (Java)** | 0.652 s **0.105 s** | 15.11 MB **16.86 MB** | **osbxl is ~6.2x faster**. POI carries heavy XML schema init overhead; osbxl starts and finishes instantly. |
| **Node.js** (v24) | ExcelJS 4.4.0 **nodeosbxl** (`setOnlyMode`) | 0.056 s **0.016 s** | 103.95 MB **121.14 MB** | **nodeosbxl is ~3.5x faster (0.016s)**. Under identical serialization mode (setOnlyMode), nodeosbxl beats ExcelJS with only 18 MB V8 heap consumption. |
| **Python** (3.14) | openpyxl 3.1.5 **pyosbxl** (`setOnlyMode`) | 0.017 s **0.016 s** | 53.20 MB 69.91 MB | Under matching write-only mode, **pyosbxl edges out openpyxl at 0.016s**. Python heap usage is kept down to just 12 MB. |
| **PHP** (8.5) | PhpSpreadsheet 5.10.0 **phposbxl** | 0.073 s **0.024 s** | 26.00 MB **2.00 MB** | **phposbxl is ~3x faster and uses 13x less memory (only 2 MB)**. Critical advantage under concurrent web downloads. |

### 3. Large-Scale 50,000-Row (200,000 Cells) Stress Test

Stress test results scaling data up to **50,000 rows × 4 columns = 200,000 cells + SUM formula**. While popular open-source libraries crash from out-of-memory errors, osbxl completes cleanly across all platforms.

| Runtime / Limits | Library | Execution Time | Memory Usage | Highlights & Fault Analysis |
|---|---|:---:|:---:|---|
| **PHP** (8.5 / 128M) | PhpSpreadsheet 5.10.0 **phposbxl** | ✕ Crashed **5.836 s** | ✕ OOM (>128MB limit) **32.00 MB** | **PhpSpreadsheet crashes fatally** (`Allowed memory size exhausted`). **phposbxl runs safely using only 32 MB** (generating a 1.93 MB .xlsx). |
| **Java** (JDK 1.8 / 256M) | Apache POI 5.2.5 (XSSF) **osbxl (Java)** | ✕ Crashed **6.394 s** | ✕ OOM (>256MB heap) **36.19 MB** | **POI crashes fatally** (`OutOfMemoryError: Java heap space`). **osbxl finishes cleanly in 6.4s within 36.19 MB** without requiring rewriting to restricted SXSSF streaming mode. |
| **Node.js** (v24) | ExcelJS 4.4.0 **nodeosbxl** (`setOnlyMode`) | 1.218 s **1.798 s** | 772.11 MB **1,836 MB** *(V8 heap: 20.9 MB)* | Under identical write-only conditions (setOnlyMode), nodeosbxl clocks in at 1.798s. While ExcelJS inflates V8 heap (>420 MB), **nodeosbxl uses only 20.9 MB of V8 heap**. |
| **Python** (3.14) | openpyxl 3.1.5 **pyosbxl** (`setOnlyMode`) | 2.500 s **1.900 s** | 377.93 MB **1,445 MB** *(Python heap: 28 MB)* | Under identical write-only conditions (setOnlyMode), **pyosbxl outperforms openpyxl at 1.900s**. Python runtime heap usage is only 28 MB. |

> 💡 **Memory Structure & Language Heap Safety**:
> ExcelJS and openpyxl keep every cell, row, and style as language-level objects in the runtime heap, rapidly consuming Node.js and Python heap limits (ExcelJS >420 MB, openpyxl >370 MB).
> In contrast, osbxl transfers 2D matrix data immediately into the C++ core engine. **Node.js V8 heap usage remains at a modest 20.9 MB for 50,000 rows, and Python heap is only 28 MB**, entirely preventing language runtime OOM heap crashes. The process Peak RSS represents temporary native working buffers used by the C++ core for multi-threaded XML generation and ZIP compression.
> 📖 **Full Feature Matrix & Detailed Analysis**: See [Excel Library Feature Comparison & Benchmark Report (en/benchmark-comparison.md)](en/benchmark-comparison.md).

---

## 🚀 Quick Code Examples

### Python (`pyosbxl`)

```python
import pyosbxl

app = pyosbxl.App()
book = app.createWorkBook("sales_report.xlsx")
sheet = book.addWorkSheet("Sales")

sheet.getRange("A1").setValue("Monthly Sales")
sheet.getRange("A2").setValue(150000)
sheet.getRange("A3").setValue(230000)
sheet.getRange("A4").setFormula("SUM(A2:A3)")

book.save()
book.close()
```

### Node.js (`nodeosbxl`)

```javascript

const app = new osbxl.App();
const book = app.createWorkBook("report.xlsx");
const sheet = book.addWorkSheet("Sheet1");

sheet.getRange("A1").setNumberValue(100);
sheet.getRange("A2").setNumberValue(200);

- 后端 `app/`：FastAPI + SQLAlchemy。`app/agents/` 是智能体核心，包括流式文件解析器 `parser.py`、静态检查 `qa.py`、各角色提示词 `prompts.py`、编排器 `pipeline.py` 和调用追踪 `tracing.py`；`app/metrics.py` 负责用量、运营和状态页的聚合。
- 前端 `web/`：Vite + React + TypeScript + Tailwind。构建产物由 FastAPI 同源托管，所以不需要处理跨域，Cookie 鉴权也最简单。

## 实现思路与关键取舍

1. **产物形态：多文件 React 项目 + Sandpack 预览。** 参考了几个开源实现：
   - bolt.diy 用 WebContainer 在浏览器里跑完整 Node 环境，但用于商业生产需要授权，体积也重。
   - E2B / Open Lovable 用云端沙箱，需要额外的付费服务和接入。
   - LlamaCoder 只生成单个组件。

   Sandpack 能在浏览器里编译多文件 React 项目，不需要服务端算力，预览运行在跨域 iframe 中，天然和主站隔离。代价是只支持纯前端应用、依赖需要白名单。

   样式方面踩过一个坑：现网探针（让预览里的代码把 ` `、脚本和计算样式 postMessage 回主页面）发现 Sandpack 的 react 模板会忽略自定义 `index.html` 的 ` `，最初放在里面的 Tailwind CDN 脚本从未生效；而且 `cdn.tailwindcss.com` 在国内网络下本身也访问不了。现在改为把官方 `@tailwindcss/browser`（v4）打包成本站静态资源，通过 Sandpack 的 `externalResources` 注入，深色模式用隐藏入口文件注册 class 变体。
2. **输出协议：流式 ` ` 标签。** 借鉴 bolt.diy，模型按 ` ... ` 输出，后端边收边解析，按文件推送事件，前端可以展示"工程师正在写哪个文件"。模型偶尔不遵守格式，因此做了三层兜底：
   - 用户消息末尾附格式示例；
   - 解析 Markdown 代码块并从上下文推断文件名；
   - 仍然没有文件时，带纠正提示自动重试一次。
3. **流式传输用 NDJSON 而不是 SSE。** 发消息的 POST 请求直接返回事件流，前端用 `fetch` + `ReadableStream` 读取。比"先 POST 再开 EventSource"少一次往返，服务端也不需要暂存运行状态。前端每帧最多渲染一次，扛得住每秒上千个代码增量事件。
4. **QA 用确定性静态检查，不调用 LLM。** 入口文件、相对引用、依赖白名单、保留文件都用规则检查，又快又稳；发现问题再交给 Alex 修一轮，避免"让 LLM 审 LLM"的成本和不确定性。用真实模型实测后又加了"引入的名字是否真的存在"：lucide-react 图标名对照随仓库附带的 `lucide-react@0.460.0` 图标表（和 Sandpack 用的版本一致；实测 glm 和 grok 都编造过不存在的 `Tomato` 图标，导致预览白屏），以及相对文件的默认导入 / 具名导入是否和导出一致。
5. **迭代时增量修改。** 小改动只让 Alex 输出变更文件，再和上一版本合并，速度快、token 少，也不容易改坏无关代码。
6. **版本是不可变快照。** 回滚 = 复制旧版本生成新版本，历史永远不会丢。
7. **默认关闭 / 压低模型的思考。** 实测 deepseek 系列开启思考时，模型会在思考阶段先把代码草拟一遍，首字延迟达到几十秒；关闭后整体快很多。GLM / Grok 不认 DeepSeek 风格的 `thinking` 参数，改为发送低思考强度（Chat 协议的 `reasoning_effort`、Responses 协议的 `reasoning.effort`）。同一个三模型 Race 实测从 479 秒、12 万 token 降到 56 秒、2 万 token。可以用 `LLM_DISABLE_THINKING=false` 打开完整思考。
8. **按模型适配协议。** 同一网关下，grok 系列只支持 Responses 协议（Chat Completions 直接返回 `protocol_not_supported`），glm-5.3 在 Chat 协议下会把思考过程混进正文，所以这两类走 Responses 协议（`LLM_RESPONSES_MODELS`），其他模型遇到 `protocol_not_supported` 时自动切换。可选参数被某个模型拒绝（400）时，逐个去掉试探，只丢掉真正被拒绝的那个，并按模型记住。追踪数据还暴露过一次静默失败：glm-5.3-flashx 不接受关闭思考，即使低思考强度也会在思考里先把整份代码写一遍，用完网关默认的 4096 输出 token 后正文为空，Race 里这一路就悄悄消失了。现在每次调用显式设置 `LLM_MAX_TOKENS`（默认 16384，被拒绝时同样自动去掉），某一路没有产出代码时明确报错，新建时没有代码则整轮报错。
9. **邀请码控制注册，账号承载身份。** 邀请码只在注册时校验并扣减次数，注册后所有鉴权、项目归属和额度都基于账号。密码用标准库 scrypt 加盐哈希，不引入额外依赖。
10. **不引入 Alembic。** 启动时 `create_all` 创建缺失的表；对已有表新增的可空列，用 `app/db.py` 里一个十几行的 `_add_missing_columns()` 检查后补 `ALTER TABLE ADD COLUMN`。发布记录用独立的 `shares` 表，不改旧表。Demo 阶段表结构简单，属于有意的复杂度控制。
11. **Race 只分叉"写代码"这一段。** PRD 和架构对两个方案是共享的，分叉在 Alex 之后，这样对比的是"同一需求的两种实现"，而不是两份不同的需求；也少跑一次 Emma 和 Bob。实现上把"Alex 编码 → QA → 修复一轮"抽成 `_code_and_check`，普通生成和 Race 共用；Race 用 `asyncio.Queue` 合并多路事件流，每个事件带 `lane` 字段，前端按 lane 分别渲染。每路产出一个 `source=race` 的候选版本，"采用"复用已有的回滚接口生成最新版本，不需要新接口。
12. **Race 的模型选择。** 所有模型走同一个 OpenAI 兼容网关，`LLM_RACE_MODELS` 只是一份白名单（`LLM_MODEL` 总会被加进去），用户在界面上勾选 2-3 个参赛，后端校验必须在白名单内。不同模型对可选参数的支持不一样（例如有的不认 DeepSeek 风格的 `thinking`，有的不认 `stream_options`），所以某个模型返回 400 时，会按顺序去掉这些可选参数重试，并对这个模型记住，之后不再发送。某一路模型报错只会让那一路失败，其他方案照常产出。不传模型时，用默认模型的两种风格（低温度稳健版 + 高温度、视觉更大胆的创意版）比较。Race 只在新建或推倒重做时生效（小修改没必要比较），每个参赛模型消耗 1 次额度——第 1 次由接口扣，其余由流水线在确定要 Race 时才扣，Mike 判断为"修改"时不会多扣；额度不够时自动退回单方案并提示。
13. **发布的是快照，不是实时同步。** 分享链接指向某个具体版本，继续修改不会影响已发布的应用，需要手动"更新到最新版本"，和 Atoms / Vercel 的发布语义一致。
14. **可观测性自建，不接第三方。** 多智能体 + 多模型的产品，最需要回答的是"这一轮慢在哪、花了多少 token、哪个模型最容易失败、服务现在是否可用"。实现分三层，见下方"可观测性与运营"一节。没有接 Langfuse 之类的平台，是为了不增加外部依赖和部署成本；表结构按 trace（`runs`）/ generation（`llm_calls`）组织，和这类平台的概念一致，之后要迁移也只需要在 `TracedLLM` 里多上报一份。
15. **演示模式是一个"假模型"，不是一条假流程。** `MockLLM` 实现和真实客户端相同的 `LLM` 接口，按系统提示词识别角色，回放预置内容：Emma / Bob 是对应应用的 PRD 和架构，Alex 按真实的 ` ` 协议分块流式输出完整的多文件 React 项目。因此解析器、QA、版本、Race、追踪都真实运行，测试里也校验了预置应用能通过 QA。主题色集中在 `/lib/theme.js`，Race 每一路用不同的强调色和明暗风格，迭代时"把主色调换成蓝色"只改这一个文件。线上用 `FallbackLLM` 包住真实客户端：调用在产出任何内容之前就失败（连接错误、401 / 403、限流或额度不足、5xx）时，本轮剩余步骤改走演示模式，并通过 `notice` 事件告诉用户；已经开始输出后再失败则照常报错，因为半截回答没法由另一个模型接着写。这样演示能否跑完不再取决于第三方网关和额度。

## 可观测性与运营

参考了 Atoms 文档里的 [积分和使用情况](https://help.atoms.dev/zh/articles/12129588-credits-and-usage)（余额常驻、使用历史）、[分析概览](https://help.atoms.dev/zh/articles/12129580-analytics-overview)（已发布站点的访问、来源、设备，7 / 30 天）。

```
run_pipeline ──tracer.wrap(llm, agent, step, lane)──▶ TracedLLM ──▶ OpenAICompatLLM
     │                                                    │
     ▼                                                    ▼
   runs（每轮：模式、状态、QA、版本、token、耗时）      llm_calls（每次调用：prompt、思考、输出、
                                                          输入 / 输出 token、首字延迟、耗时、成败）
```

- **追踪**：`TracedLLM` 包住任意 LLM（测试里的假 LLM 也一样），记录每次调用；格式重试记为 `alex-retry`，QA 修复轮记为 `alex-fix`，Race 每路带 `lane`。客户端中途断开时，这一轮和进行中的调用记为"中断"，不算作失败。追踪数据交给单个后台线程按顺序写入：线上数据库每次往返有几百毫秒，同步写入会拖慢下一个智能体，还会阻塞事件循环、卡住其他用户的请求；写入失败只记日志，不影响生成，进程退出前会把队列写完。单个文本字段超过 10 万字符会截断。
- **用户层**：工作台每轮结束显示耗时、token 和各角色的 token，点"查看明细"打开时间线抽屉（每次调用的起止时间、首字延迟、输入 / 输出 token，可展开思考过程和输出）。顶栏常驻剩余额度，点进 `/usage` 看 7 / 30 天的运行、成功率、token 趋势、按模型 / 按角色拆分和最近运行。发布弹窗里有近 7 天访问量、来源和设备占比。
- **管理员层**（`ADMIN_USERNAMES` 指定）：`/admin` 展示用户 / 项目 / 运行量、成功率、耗时 P50 / P95、token；模型健康度（调用数、失败率、平均和 P95 首字延迟）；各角色 token 占比；生成质量（QA 最终通过率、需要修复轮的比例、Race 次数和被采用次数；采用次数只统计追踪上线之后，和 Race 次数口径一致）；活跃用户、额度预警、邀请码使用、热门分享；运行记录可按状态、模型、用户筛选，打开后能看到完整的 system / user prompt。
- **公开状态页** `/status`：应用、数据库（`SELECT 1` 延迟）、模型网关（`models.list` 探测，缓存 60 秒）三个组件的状态，近 24 小时生成成功率和每小时分布、各模型的调用成功率与首字延迟、版本号和运行时长。数据库不可用为"服务中断"；网关不可用，或近 24 小时成功率低于 80%（至少 5 轮）时为"性能下降"。不返回任何用户数据。`/healthz` 保持轻量，仍用于部署和容器健康检查。
- **隐私边界**：prompt 原文只有管理员能看；普通用户的明细里只有自己这一轮的思考过程和输出，不含系统提示词。

线上实测（2026-10-11，deepseek-flash）：追踪数据暴露了一个此前没注意到的瓶颈。最初一轮"番茄钟"新建 22.6 秒，三次模型调用只占约 12.5 秒，其余时间都花在数据库往返上：应用部署在香港，Neon 数据库却在 `us-east-2`，`/status` 显示 `SELECT 1` 稳定在约 650 ms。分两步解决：

| 阶段 | 一轮新建总耗时 | 模型调用以外的耗时 | 数据库 `SELECT 1` |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 追踪同步写库，数据库在美国 | 22.6 秒 | 约 10 秒 | 约 650 ms |
| 追踪改为后台线程写入 | 21.2 秒 | 约 6.4 秒 | 约 650 ms |
| 数据库迁到新加坡（`aws-ap-southeast-1`） | 14.8 秒 | 约 1.5 秒 | 约 120 ms |

迁移方式：新建新加坡区域的 Neon 项目，在服务器上演练一次 `pg_dump` / `pg_restore` 并核对 9 张表行数；正式切换时先停应用、再导出导入、核对一致后改 `DATABASE_URL` 启动，停机 55 秒，登录态和数据都不受影响。美国区域的旧项目保留为备份（不再写入），服务器上也留有切换时的导出文件。

🎙️ Voice in · 🧠 Local AI · 🔊 Voice out · 🗃️ Persistent memory · ⏰ Smart reminders
  Privacy-first and self-hosted: text and voice conversations run through your own services, without cloud AI APIs.

13. [Known Limitations & Roadmap](#known-limitations--roadmap)

---

## Features

- 🎙️ **Voice in, voice out**: send a Telegram voice note, get a text reply plus an MP3 audio reply.
- 📝 **Local speech-to-text**: `faster-whisper-small` served by [Speaches](https://github.com/speaches-ai/speaches).
- 🔊 **Local text-to-speech**: `Kokoro-82M` (ONNX) via Speaches.
- 🧠 **Local LLM**: any Ollama chat model (default: `richardyoung/qwen2.5-3b-instruct-abliterated`).
- 🗃️ **Persistent memory**: last 10 messages per conversation are sent as context.
- ⏰ **Natural-language reminders**: "remind me to call John at 5pm" is parsed by the LLM into structured JSON and saved.
- ⚙️ **Reliable reminder dispatcher**: cron workflow runs every minute and uses `FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED` to avoid double-sending.
- 🛡️ **Safety rails**: update de-duplication, per-user rate limiting (10 msgs / 60 s), `/register` gate, error alerts to an admin chat.
- 🚨 **Centralized error handling**: any failing workflow notifies you on Telegram.

---

## Architecture

```
                    ┌──────────────────────────────┐
  Telegram user ──▶ │  Telegram Trigger            │
                    └──────────────┬───────────────┘
                                   ▼
                       Dedup (processed_updates)
                                   ▼
                          Voice note attached?
                     ┌─────────────┴──────────────┐
                    YES                           NO
                     ▼                             ▼
        Download voice file                 Has text?  ──no──▶ "text only" notice
                     ▼                             ▼
     Speaches STT (faster-whisper)         Rate-limit check
                     ▼                             ▼
            Rate-limit check               User upsert ─▶ /register? ─▶ mark registered
                     ▼                             ▼
              User upsert                  Registered? ──no──▶ "please /register"
                     ▼                             ▼
          Registered gate                 contains "remind"?
                     ▼                    ┌────────┴─────────┐
        Ensure conversation              YES                 NO
                     ▼                    ▼                   ▼
          Load last 10 messages    Ollama extracts       Ensure conversation
                     ▼              {content, due_at}            ▼
              Ollama chat                 ▼               Load history ─▶ Ollama chat
              ┌──────┴───────┐      Save to reminders              ▼
              ▼              ▼            ▼                 Text reply ─▶ log messages
         Text reply    Speaches TTS   Confirm to user
              ▼              ▼
        Log messages    Audio reply (mp3)

  ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
  │ Reminder Dispatcher (every 1 min)                          │
  │ claim due reminders ─▶ send Telegram ─▶ mark sent / failed │
  └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

  ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
  │ Error Handler: Error Trigger ─▶ Telegram alert to admin    │
  └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

├── README.md
└── workflows/
    ├── chatbot-v2-voice-activated.json   # Main bot: text, voice, reminders, memory
    ├── reminder-dispatcher-cron.json     # Scheduled reminder delivery

## Tech Stack

| Component | Purpose |
|-----------|---------|
| [n8n](https://n8n.io) | Workflow automation engine |
| Telegram Bot API | User interface |
| [Ollama](https://ollama.com) | Local LLM inference (`/api/chat`) |
| [Speaches](https://github.com/speaches-ai/speaches) | OpenAI-compatible STT/TTS server |

## Prerequisites

- A running **n8n** instance (self-hosted, v1.x recent enough for Postgres node 2.6 and IF node 2.3).
- A **Telegram bot token** from [@BotFather](https://t.me/BotFather).
- A **PostgreSQL** database reachable from n8n.
- **Ollama** reachable from n8n, with your chosen model pulled.
- **Speaches** reachable from n8n (the workflow uses the hostname `speaches` on port `8000`, so run it on the same Docker network, or change the URL).
- Your n8n instance must be reachable over **HTTPS** by Telegram (required for the Telegram Trigger webhook).

---

## Installation & Setup

### 1. 🚀 Start supporting services

Example `docker-compose.yml` fragment (adapt to your environment):

```yaml
services:
  speaches:
    image: ghcr.io/speaches-ai/speaches:latest-cpu
    container_name: speaches
    ports:
      - "8000:8000"
    restart: unless-stopped
    # Put on the same network as n8n so http://speaches:8000 resolves
```

Pull the Ollama model on the Ollama host:

```bash
ollama pull richardyoung/qwen2.5-3b-instruct-abliterated
```

Download the speech models into Speaches (once):

```bash
curl -X POST http://speaches:8000/v1/models/Systran/faster-whisper-small
curl -X POST http://speaches:8000/v1/models/speaches-ai/Kokoro-82M-v1.0-ONNX
```

> The main workflow includes a disconnected helper node (`HTTP Request`) that performs the Whisper model download. Run it manually once if you prefer to do it from n8n.

### 2. 🗃️ Create the database

Run the SQL in [Database Schema](#database-schema) against your PostgreSQL database.

### 3. 🔐 Create n8n credentials

In n8n, go to **Credentials** and create:

| Credential | Type | Notes |
|------------|------|-------|
| `Telegram account` | Telegram API | Bot token from BotFather |
| `Postgres account` | Postgres | Host, port, DB, user, password |

### 4. 🔄 Import the workflows

For each file in `workflows/`: **n8n → Workflows → Import from file**.

After import, open every Telegram and Postgres node and **select your credential** (they were stripped for security). The quickest way: open the workflow, click a node showing a credential warning, choose the credential, repeat.

### 5. ⚙️ Configure the workflows

1. **Error Handler**: in the *Send a text message* node, replace `YOUR_TELEGRAM_ADMIN_CHAT_ID` with your own Telegram chat ID (get it from [@userinfobot](https://t.me/userinfobot)).
2. **Main bot** (`ChatBot-v2`): update the Ollama URL (`http://10.0.3.1:11434`) in the three HTTP Request nodes (`HTTP Request2`, `HTTP Request3`, `Ask Ollama (Voice)`) to your Ollama host, and the model name if different.
3. **Reminder Dispatcher**: check the timezone in workflow settings (default `Asia/Karachi`).
4. In the main bot workflow settings, set **Error Workflow** to `2.Chatbot – Error Handler`. Do the same for the Reminder Dispatcher.

### 6. ✅ Activate

Activate all three workflows. Message your bot, send `/register`, then start chatting.

## Workflows in Detail

### 1. `ChatBot-v2` (main bot)

**Entry**: `Telegram Trigger1` (message updates).

**Step 1: De-duplication.** `Dedup check1` inserts `update_id` into `processed_updates` with `ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING RETURNING`. Duplicate deliveries return no row, so the run stops.

**Step 2: Routing.** `Has Voice?` splits voice notes from everything else.

**Voice path**

| Node | Action |
|------|--------|
| Get Voice File | Downloads the `.ogg` from Telegram |
| Transcribe Voice | `POST speaches:8000/v1/audio/transcriptions` (faster-whisper-small) |
| Voice Rate Limit Check / Gate | Max 10 user messages in 60 s |
| Voice User Upsert | Creates or updates the user by `telegram_chat_id` |
| Voice Registered Gate | Blocks unregistered users |
| Ensure Conversation (Voice) → Get Active Conversation → Get Recent History | Loads context (last 10 messages) |
| Build Chat Payload (Voice) | Builds system prompt + history + transcribed text |
| Ask Ollama (Voice) | Generates the reply |
| Reply Text / Synthesize Reply | Sends text reply and generates MP3 via Kokoro TTS in parallel |
| Reply Audio (Voice) | Sends the MP3 to the user |
| Log User/Assistant Message (Voice) | Persists both turns |

**Text path**

`Has Text?` → `Execute a SQL query3` (rate limit) → `If4` → `Insert or update rows in a table1` (user upsert) → `R` (`/register` command) → `Is registered?1` → `Reminder1` (message contains "remind")

repositories.description: Readable 25.7M-parameter GLM-5.3-Flash-style Hybrid-MoE built from scratch in PyTorch. Features hybrid linear/sparse attention, executable-reward RLOO, and recursive self-improvement on verified programs.
repositories.readmeExcerpt:
# Build a GLM-Style Hybrid-MoE Model From Scratch — With Recursive Self-Improvement

A readable 25.7M-parameter language model inspired by GLM-5.3-Flash: pretrained from random initialization on a synthetic Python corpus, improved with executable-reward RLOO, then improved again by a **recursive self-improvement ladder that trains the model on its own verified programs**. Includes a GLM-faithful miniature vision path, CPU-scale research experiments, an interactive slide deck, and SHA-256-audited receipts for every run. CUDA, Apple Silicon MPS, and CPU.

Self-improvement ladder

## Headline result (real runs, receipts included)

The pretrained model solved 5 of 6 held-out coding families greedily. A recursive self-improvement ladder targeting the failing family (`even`) sampled completions, kept only the ones that passed the executable verifier, and fine-tuned on them:

| | Held-out `even` | Other 5 families | Total |
|---|---|---|---|
| Pretrained step-150 | 0/2 | 5 passing | 5/6 |
| After RSI cycle 1 (2 verified programs) | **1/2** | 0 passing | 1/6 |
| After RSI cycle 3 (4 verified programs) | **1/2** | 2 passing | 3/6 |

The model taught itself a new family from 4 self-generated, machine-verified programs — and forgot three others doing it (catastrophic interference, measured and visible in `EXAMPLES.md`: it started emitting `x % 2 ==== 0` for `square`). Both effects are the result; neither is hidden. See [`REPORT.md`](REPORT.md).

## What was built

| Component | Released GLM-5.3-Flash | This project |
|---|---:|---:|
| Total parameters | 320B | 25,730,592 |
| Active parameters/token | 18B | 9,805,344 |
| Layers | 45 | 12 (9 linear + 3 sparse attention) |
| Attention | hybrid linear/sparse, KDA | ELU+1 linear + gathered sparse |
| Routed experts | 288, top-8 | 8, top-2 + 1 shared |
| Residual streams | multi-stream mHC | 4 learned streams, simplified |
| Tokenizer | BPE, 154,880 | raw UTF-8 bytes, 260 |
| Context | up to 1M | 192 bytes |
| Modalities | text, image, video | text + fixed 32×32 RGB |

## The three training stages

```text
1. PRETRAIN   next-byte prediction on procedural Python; 150 steps: loss 5.55 -> 0.43
2. RLOO       policy gradient with executable reward (leave-one-out baseline)
3. RSI        recursive self-improvement:
                propose  -> sample K completions per task
                verify   -> keep only completions that pass every hidden test
                distill  -> add to cumulative, deduplicated verified memory
                retrain  -> fine-tune on the model's own verified programs
                evaluate -> greedy pass@1 on frozen held-out tasks
                escalate -> (optional) unlock the next family rung
```

The verifier (`glm_mini/evaluator.py`) is fail-closed: one function, no imports/loops/attributes/recursion, allowlisted calls only, hidden tests in a restricted namespace. That gate is what makes self-generated data honest.

## Quick start

```bash
cd glm-mini-from-scratch
python3.12 -m venv .venv
source .venv/bin/activate        # Windows: .venv\Scripts\activate
python -m pip install -r requirements.txt
python -m pytest -q              # 37 tests
```

## Run everything

Windows (`run_cpu.bat`) and bash (`run_gpu.sh`) wrappers handle the venv for you:

```bash
# 1. pretrain (about 9 min CPU)
run_cpu.bat scripts\train_pretrain.py --output runs\pretrain-001 --steps 150 --checkpoints 50,100,150 --batch-size 16 --seed 42

# 2. recursive self-improvement on the failing family
run_cpu.bat scripts\train_self_improve.py --initial-checkpoint runs\pretrain-001\checkpoint-0150 --output runs\self-improve-even-001 --cycles 3 --families-ladder even --seed 73

# 3. charts from the receipts
run_cpu.bat scripts\make_charts.py --output artifacts\charts --pretrain-receipt runs\pretrain-001\training-receipt.json --self-improve-receipt runs\self-improve-even-001\training-receipt.json
```

Bash equivalents live in `scripts/`: `run_self_improvement.sh`, `run_rl_variant_screen.sh`, `run_experiment_suite.sh` (plus `.bat` twins for Windows).

## Evaluation

```bash
run_cpu.bat scripts\evaluate.py --checkpoint runs\self-improve-even-001\checkpoint-cycle-03 --split confirm --per-family 1 --families even,reverse,square,absolute,nonnegative,list_sum --output runs\confirm-after.json
run_cpu.bat scripts\evaluate_passk.py --checkpoint ... --split confirm --samples 8 --output runs\passk.json
```

## Vision path

A faithful miniature of the released image topology — RGB patch embedding, two bidirectional ViT blocks, learned 2×2 spatial merge, gated projector — splices 16 visual tokens into the byte sequence. Measured on generated digits (200 held-out):

| Architecture | After training |
|---|---:|
| GLM-faithful tower | 109/200 (54.5%) |
| Direct-patch baseline (labeled control) | 187/200 (93.5%) |

A bounded pilot attached the tower to the full 12-layer coding model and reached **45/100** held-out while training only 2.3M of 25.8M parameters. Details and honest caveats: [`VISION_REPORT.md`](VISION_REPORT.md), [`MULTIMODAL.md`](MULTIMODAL.md).

## Research experiments

CPU-scale matched studies with paired-seed analysis (`scripts/run_experiment_suite.sh` / `.bat`):

- **Data diversity** — 8 vs 32 vs 88 unique compositional structures at fixed compute. At this budget: no significant difference (reported, not spun).
- **Ordering & curriculum** — identical examples, interleaved vs blocked vs 8→88 curriculum. Interleaved led both seeds.
- **RL design screen** — one changed choice per arm, exact McNemar + Holm correction (`scripts/analyze_rl_variants.py`); a screen selects candidates, it does not establish results.
- **Vision pilot** — full-model integration with a bounded trainable surface.

Receipts and analyses: `artifacts/experiments/`, `artifacts/receipts/`.

## Slides

```bash
python slides/serve_slides.py --port 8765
# open http://127.0.0.1:8765/slides/slides.html
```

## Repository map

**Core (`glm_mini/`)**
- `model.py` — hybrid attention, MoE, residual streams, tied-head LM
- `self_improve.py` — the recursive self-improvement engine
- `vision.py` — GLM-style vision tower, projector, baseline
- `tasks.py` / `evaluator.py` / `tokenizer.py` / `runtime.py` — data, verifier, bytes, checkpoints + generation

**Scripts** — `train_pretrain.py`, `train_rl.py`, `train_self_improve.py`, `train_vision.py`, `evaluate.py`, `evaluate_passk.py`, `make_charts.py`, `analyze_rl_variants.py`

**Experiments** — `pretraining_data_diversity.py`, `pretraining_curriculum_order.py`, `full_25m_vision_digit_pilot.py`, plus analyzers

**Docs** — [`TUTORIAL.md`](TUTORIAL.md) (beginner course), [`REPORT.md`](REPORT.md) (method + results), [`EXAMPLES.md`](EXAMPLES.md) (real generations), [`VISION_REPORT.md`](VISION_REPORT.md), [`MULTIMODAL.md`](MULTIMODAL.md)

## Design rules

- **Determinism** — explicit seeds everywhere; tasks from pure integer hashes.
- **Fail-closed** — no overwrites; NaN hard-fails; unknown splits rejected.
- **Receipts** — versioned JSON with SHA-256 weight hashes for every entry point.
- **Device** — `--device auto` resolves cuda → mps → cpu; bf16 autocast only on CUDA.

## Limitations

25M parameters, 192-byte context, synthetic benchmark, single-seed comparisons at teaching scale. Self-improvement interference is documented, not solved. This is a teaching artifact: it establishes method, not broad ability.

**Renew SSL certificates on every server, safely.**

[CI](https://github.com/ilramdhan/sslsync/actions/workflows/ci.yml)

[**Documentation**](https://ilramdhan.github.io/sslsync/) · [Quick start](https://ilramdhan.github.io/sslsync/getting-started/quickstart/) · [Releases](https://github.com/ilramdhan/sslsync/releases)

---

**sslsync** puts a new SSL/TLS certificate on all your servers from one laptop. It checks every server first, replaces the files, reloads the services, and **proves** each port serves the new certificate. If anything fails, it puts the old certificate back by itself.

- **One file to configure**: hosts, ports, paths and passwords all go in `.env`. Typos are reported.
- **Checked before, verified after**: SSH, sudo, service health, paths and permissions are checked first. Afterwards every port is compared byte for byte with the new certificate.
- **Automatic rollback**: files, Kubernetes secrets and permissions are restored, and services are reloaded.
- **Works with what you run**: Nginx, Apache, HAProxy, MinIO, PostgreSQL, Kubernetes secrets, plain files. Several on one server.
- **Auditable**: a log per run and per server, plus `summary.json`.

## Install

```bash
curl -fsSL https://ilramdhan.github.io/sslsync/install.sh | sh
```

Other ways: `brew install --cask ilramdhan/tap/sslsync`, `go install github.com/ilramdhan/sslsync/cmd/sslsync@latest`, `.deb`/`.rpm`/`.apk`, or Docker `ghcr.io/ilramdhan/sslsync`. See [Installation](docs/getting-started/installation.md).

## Use

```bash
mkdir ~/ssl-renewal && cd ~/ssl-renewal
sslsync init              # creates .env with explained examples, and certs/

# put fullchain.crt + private key in certs/, describe your servers in .env, then:
sslsync list              # how .env was understood (+ typo warnings)
sslsync validate          # is the certificate OK?
sslsync check             # read-only check of every server
sslsync deploy --only web-staging    # one server first
sslsync deploy --group prod
sslsync status            # every port NEW?
```

A server in `.env` looks like this:

```bash
SSLSYNC_SERVERS=WEB_PROD
DEFAULT_CERT_FILE=certs/example.com/fullchain.crt
DEFAULT_KEY_FILE=certs/example.com/example.com.key

WEB_PROD_HOST=web.example.com
WEB_PROD_USER=deploy
WEB_PROD_PASSWORD='…'
WEB_PROD_TARGETS=nginx
WEB_PROD_NGINX_CERT=/etc/ssl/certs/example.com.crt
WEB_PROD_NGINX_KEY=/etc/ssl/private/example.com.key
WEB_PROD_VERIFY=:443
```

repositories.readmeExcerpt:
# AwwO Canvas

The open-source edition of **AwwO**'s agent canvas: an infinite canvas of agent nodes with typed
input/output contracts, an orchestrator that plans, routes and runs them, and a small HTTP
protocol through which any agent engine plugs in, and unplugs, while everything keeps running.

> **中文简介**：AwwO Canvas 是 AwwO 智能体画布的开源版。它开放三部分：**画布框架**（文档模型、
> 类型化端口连线、输入输出契约、整图运行、互审 Graph、节点团队）、**编排 skill**（画布规划、
> 助手路由、节点交付格式、团队协作四种模式，全部是可热更新的 Markdown）、**热插拔执行器架构**
> （任何实现 worker 协议的进程都能随时接入或拔出，已开始的运行不会被中途换引擎）。
> 自带离线 Mock 执行器，不配置任何模型也能把整条链路跑通。设计思路见
> [docs/design.zh-CN.md](docs/design.zh-CN.md)。

The canvas after the assistant planned three nodes and the graph ran

## What is inside

| Part | Where | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Canvas framework | `packages/core`, `apps/web/src/canvas` | The document model, typed ports and wires, contracts, the closed plan protocol, graph execution, review graphs and node teams. Taken from AwwO, with AwwO's own tests. |
| Orchestration skills | `skills/*/SKILL.md` | Every prompt the orchestrator sends: the canvas planner, the assistant router, node delivery formats and team collaboration. Edit a file and the next call uses it. |
| Orchestrator | `apps/server` | Routes each assistant message (plan or execute), streams plans, runs graphs and node teams, and owns the hot-plug runtime registry. |
| Runtimes | `workers/`, `runtimes.json` | Reference workers: an offline **mock**, an **OpenAI-compatible** worker for any Chat Completions API, and a standard-library **Python** worker. |

## Quick start

Requires Node.js 22.12 or newer.

```bash
git clone https://github.com/Boxpo/awwo-canvas.git
cd awwo-canvas
npm install
npm run dev
```

Open [http://127.0.0.1:5173](http://127.0.0.1:5173). `npm run dev` starts the mock worker (`:8791`),
the orchestrator (`:8787`) and the canvas dev server (`:5173`), all bound to `127.0.0.1`. Ask the
assistant for something ("在画布上搭建：咖啡订阅上线页面，撰写后由评审验收"), or load an example from
the **Canvas** menu, then press **Run graph**. The mock answers in the exact shape of every node's
output contract, so plans, graph runs, review loops and teams all complete offline.

One process instead of three, the way you would run it on a machine:

```bash
npm run build          # builds the canvas into apps/web/dist
npm run worker:mock    # in one terminal
npm start              # in another: canvas and API on http://127.0.0.1:8787
```

### Use a real model

The OpenAI-compatible worker speaks to OpenAI, vLLM, Ollama, LM Studio, one-api/new-api relays and
other Chat Completions endpoints. Its key stays in the worker process; the orchestrator and the
browser never see it.

```bash
# macOS / Linux
AWWO_OPENAI_API_KEY=sk-... AWWO_OPENAI_BASE_URL=https://api.openai.com/v1 AWWO_OPENAI_MODELS=gpt-4.1-mini npm run dev
```

```powershell
# Windows PowerShell
$env:AWWO_OPENAI_API_KEY = "sk-..."; $env:AWWO_OPENAI_MODELS = "gpt-4.1-mini"; npm run dev
```

Then choose the `openai` runtime on a node, or make it the default for everything:
`AWWO_DEFAULT_RUNTIME=openai`, `AWWO_PLANNER_RUNTIME=openai`, `AWWO_ROUTER_RUNTIME=openai`.
Every variable is listed in [.env.example](.env.example).

## How it fits together

```text
 browser · apps/web                 orchestrator · apps/server                 workers · any language
┌──────────────────────────┐ /api ┌──────────────────────────────────┐ protocol v1 ┌──────────────────┐
│ canvas document           │─────▶│ assistant router  (plan|execute)  │────────────▶│ mock             │
│ (@awwo/core)              │ SSE  │ planner · graph runs · teams      │ GET /health │ openai-compatible│
│ plan → validate → apply   │◀─────│ review loop · direct runs         │ POST /runs  │ python-minimal   │
│ as ONE undo step          │      │ runtime registry  (hot-plug)      │ SSE events  │ your engine      │
└──────────────────────────┘      │ skills/*.md       (hot-reload)    │             └──────────────────┘
                                   └──────────────────────────────────┘
```

- **The document is the source of truth.** Nodes, wires, contracts and the review policy live in
  one canvas document in the browser. The planner only *proposes* operations from a closed
  protocol; the canvas validates them against the current document and applies them as a single
  undoable change, or reports the proposal stale if the canvas moved meanwhile.
- **The orchestrator owns runs.** A graph run gets a frozen copy of the document, resolves every
  node's runtime and model at admission, and streams numbered events, so a reload or a dropped
  connection resumes where it left off.
- **Workers are processes, not SDKs.** The orchestrator links no agent SDK. It routes each model
  call to the worker named by the node's runtime over a four-endpoint HTTP protocol.

The full design, and why each rule exists, is in [docs/design.md](docs/design.md).

## Hot-plug runtimes

A runtime is any process that speaks [worker protocol v1](packages/core/src/protocol.ts):

| Endpoint | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `GET /health` | The catalog: models, input budgets, reasoning-effort levels, tools, capacity |
| `POST /internal/runs` | One model call, streamed as `text_delta` / `reasoning` / `completed` / `failed` / `cancelled` events |
| `DELETE /internal/runs/{runId}` | Stop that call (idempotent) |
| `POST /internal/completions` | One-shot call, used by the assistant router |

Three ways to plug one in, none of which restarts anything:

1. List it in `runtimes.json`. The file is watched; edits apply immediately.
2. `POST /api/runtimes` with `{ "id", "url", "label"?, "token"? }`, or use **Runtimes → Plug in** in the canvas.
3. Start the worker with `AWWO_REGISTER_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8787` and it registers itself
   (`python workers/python-minimal/worker.py` also unregisters on exit).

The registry probes every worker, checks that its catalog is well formed and that it serves the
runtime id it was registered under, and marks it unavailable when it stops answering. A run keeps
the runtime and model it was admitted with: unplugging a worker never silently moves a running
node to another engine. To write your own worker, start from
[workers/mock/worker.mjs](workers/mock/worker.mjs) (dependency-free, about 260 lines) or
[workers/python-minimal/worker.py](workers/python-minimal/worker.py).

## Orchestration skills

| Skill | Used for |
| --- | --- |
| [canvas-planner](skills/canvas-planner/SKILL.md) | Turns a goal into a version-1 plan: nodes from seven role templates, contracts, wires and an optional review policy |
| [assistant-router](skills/assistant-router/SKILL.md) | Decides whether a message edits the canvas (`plan`) or is a task to do now (`execute`); explicit canvas wording is routed by rule, anything unclear falls back to `plan` |
| [node-delivery](skills/node-delivery/SKILL.md) | How a node must answer its output contract: one text field, keyed JSON, complete HTML, file references |
| [team-orchestration](skills/team-orchestration/SKILL.md) | Deterministic teams of 1-8 members inside one node: sequential, parallel, debate and review |

Each skill is Markdown with named `### block:  ` sections. The orchestrator reloads a skill
when its file changes; runs that already started keep the text they were admitted with. A
required block that is missing stops the server at start-up rather than falling back to other
wording.

## Commands

| Command | |
| --- | --- |
| `npm run dev` | Mock worker + orchestrator + canvas dev server (the OpenAI worker too when a key is set) |
| `npm test` | Unit and integration tests for core, server, web and the workers |
| `npm run typecheck` | TypeScript across the workspace |
| `npm run build` | Production build of the canvas |
| `npm run smoke` | Offline end-to-end check: boots the real orchestrator with mock workers and drives the HTTP API the canvas uses |

## Security

AwwO Canvas is a single-user tool that spends model credentials through its workers.

- Every process binds to `127.0.0.1`. The orchestrator refuses a non-loopback bind unless
  `AWWO_API_TOKEN` is set, and then requires `Authorization: Bearer  ` on `/api`.
- Writes from a foreign browser origin are refused, and the `Host` header is checked against the
  names the server answers to, which blocks DNS-rebinding pages.
- Worker URLs and tokens are orchestrator configuration only. They never enter a canvas document,
  an exported file or anything sent to the browser.
- HTML deliverables are previewed in a sandboxed iframe with no capabilities, under a strict CSP.

There are no user accounts. Do not expose the orchestrator to a network you do not control.

## Provenance and license

Cut from AwwO at upstream commit `9376e770` as a standalone repository; what came from where, and
what was changed on purpose, is listed in [NOTICE.md](NOTICE.md). MIT licensed, see [LICENSE](LICENSE).

It provides a set of pre-configured, loosely coupled platform services optimized to work interchangeably with either Docker or Podman.

It abstracts complex orchestration down to simple automation layers, allowing you to instantly spin up independent, ready-to-scale platform components.

By decoupling the runtime services, this boilerplate ensures your primary application layer connects seamlessly to its supporting infrastructure components via standard local orchestration.

This repository provides a consistent framework for local development that mirrors production environments. In production, APIs run on cloud instances (AWS, Azure, GCP) or Kubernetes pods. Meanwhile, the database layer resides on managed services like AWS RDS, Azure Database, or GCP Cloud SQL, utilizing Multi-AZ deployments for high availability and read replicas to scale performance. This streamlines the entire lifecycle—from building to monitoring—allowing teams to innovate faster.

##   Orchestration & Platform Specifics

### Supported Operating Systems

Linux
MacOS
Windows
Windows WSL2

* **Linux** (Native)
* **macOS** (Intel & Apple Silicon M1–M5)
* **Windows 10 / 11** (Most recommended via WSL2 or Hyper-V)

### Minimum Hardware Requirements

By default, local development environments run a minimal stack and do not process live production traffic. Therefore, resource utilization remains low. 

| Machine       | Machine's minimum characteristics to run this repository                                          |
| ------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| CPU           | x86_64 / ARM64 - Supports modern Intel, AMD, and Apple Silicon chips.                             |
| RAM           | 1 GB - Scale up if compiling memory-heavy stacks (e.g., Java, Angular).                           |
| DISK          | 5 GB available space - Actual usage depends on downloaded container images and project cache.     |

💡 **Tip 1 - Resource Management:** Properly restricting container CPU and memory allocations prevents resource starvation on your local host machine and closely mirrors production security best practices.

💡 **Tip 2 - Environment Separation:** The automation commands provided in this repository are optimized for local development. In production or staging environments, standard cloud infrastructure designs typically distribute these platforms across separate VPS or cloud instances rather than running them all via a single local orchestration layer. To see how these components are isolated for production, you can find the individual single-service platforms listed under my [GitHub Repositories Profile](https://github.com/pabloripoll?tab=repositories).

### Task Automation (GNU Make)

GNU

It is highly recommended to use **GNU Make** on local to manage automated workflows from the root directory. On remote, you most probably choose bash script with or without a instance personalized Makefile.

* **Recommended:** Ensure make is installed on your host system to use shortened convenience commands.
* **Alternative:** If make is unavailable, commands must be executed manually within their respective subdirectories.

### Environment Variables for Automation

The automation layer dynamically adapts commands using variables defined in your root `.env` file. These variables control how your environment invokes the runtime engine.

This repository supports local development using either **Docker** or **Podman**. You can configure your preferred container engine in your root `.env` file *(copied from `.env.example`)*: 

```sh
# ENGINE DEFINITION (docker or podman)
CONTAINER_ENGINE=docker                                 #   #

# CONTAINER VARIABLES FOR AUTOMATION
SUDO=sudo                                               #   #
DOCKER=$(SUDO) $(CONTAINER_ENGINE)                      #   #
DOCKER_COMPOSE=$(SUDO) $(CONTAINER_ENGINE) compose      #   #
```

These abstractions allow the root Makefile to trigger standard shortcuts (e.g., `make up`, `make down`) seamlessly across different setups.

⚠️ **A Note on Variable Naming:** To preserve backward compatibility with previous releases, this repository retains the use of `DOCKER` and `DOCKER_COMPOSE` as variable names throughout the codebase, scripts, and automation files. Rest assured, if you set `CONTAINER_ENGINE=podman`, these variables will correctly map to your **Podman setup** behind the scenes.

## Multi-Engine Architecture

Docker
Podman

The magic happens because modern Podman builds natively include the podman compose subcommand. It intercepts your standard, unmodified multi-container docker-compose.yml blueprints and automatically translates them down to Podman specifications.

Because this repository abstracts commands like `$ sudo docker compose up -d` via the root `Makefile` using the environment variables like `($(DOCKER_COMPOSE))`, the custom automation orchestration *(gmake/make recipes)* will point cleanly to **Podman** behind the scenes. No translation layers or custom rewrites needed.

This repository relies on a standard multi-container design (docker-compose.yml). You do not need to maintain multiple orchestration blueprints to switch engines:

- **Docker Native:** Runs commands through the standard dockerd daemon.

- **Podman Compatibility:** Modern versions of Podman include a built-in podman compose engine. When CONTAINER_ENGINE=podman is selected, Podman intercepts the docker-compose.yml specifications and automatically translates them into a Podman native configuration. No third-party translation tools are required.

#### Linux & Windows (WSL2)

Ensure your chosen container daemon is installed and running. If your local user account belongs to the docker or podman security group (allowing rootless container operations), you should set SUDO= to a blank value in your .env file.

# Horizun Civil 3D MCP

The bridge between Codex, Claude (or any MCP client) and a running **Autodesk Civil 3D**, by Horizun Group.

It is a product of its own, separate from Horizun Revit MCP, but it keeps the same contract:

v0.9.2 includes surface deviation/tolerance/RMSE comparisons, corridor targets and
guarded split/merge, region/material quantity estimates, editable COGO CSV and
explicitly refreshed alignment-linked viewports. Terrain export carries an exact
OBJ mesh with a separate Revit rollback receiver. See [engineering evidence](docs/CIVIL3D.md);
these additions have native fixture evidence on Civil 3D 2025. See the
[acceptance report](docs/ACCEPTANCE_20261005.md) for results and limits.

- **Typed tools never report work they did not verify.** Every typed write is re-read from the drawing in a new transaction
  after the commit. If the drawing does not hold what was asked for, the call is an error, even when nothing threw.
- **Typed writes are dry runs by default.** A dry run returns the plan and a single-use `confirmation_token`. The token
  is bound to the drawing, to the exact request and to the plan it resolved. You apply the write with
  `dry_run=false` plus that token.
- **Everything is resolved before the transaction.** A missing or ambiguous name is refused, and the refusal
  lists the candidates. Nothing is guessed.
- **One Civil 3D operation at a time.** Requests go through a bounded FIFO queue. If Civil 3D is busy (a command
  or a modal dialog is open), the call is refused with "busy" and nothing runs. The bridge never sends ESC.
- **Units are explicit.** Every answer states the drawing's linear, area and volume units.
- **No network listener.** The bridge only uses a local named pipe, restricted to the current user, plus a
  256-bit token.

```
Claude / MCP client
      |  MCP over stdio
horizun-civil3d-mcp.exe          (src/Horizun.Civil3D.Server)
      |  named pipe "Horizun.Civil3D- - " + token (server pid checked before sending)
Horizun.Civil3D.dll in acad.exe  (src/Horizun.Civil3D.Plugin)
      |  RequestGate (FIFO, 16) -> main thread, application context -> DocumentLock -> Transaction
Civil 3D .NET API (AeccDbMgd) + AutoCAD .NET API
```

## Tools (v0.9.2, 28 tools and 163 declared actions)

## Install (people who use it)

Codex/Claude plugin manifests, setup/workflow skills and a Claude Desktop `.mcpb`
builder are now included. The launcher exposes installation/status tools when
the matching runtime is missing. See [plugin installation and packaging](docs/PLUGIN_INSTALL.md).
Engineering v0.9.1 was installed and native-tested locally. v0.9.2 disables automatic
UNDO after a new attribution failure; see [public readiness](docs/PUBLIC_READINESS.md).

Download the latest `horizun-civil3d-mcp- .zip` from this repository's **Releases** page. Nothing is compiled
on your machine and you do not need the source or the .NET SDK.

1. Save your drawings and close every Civil 3D window.
2. Extract the zip and, inside the extracted folder, run:

```powershell
powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File .\install.ps1 -RegisterClaudeDesktop -RegisterTrustedPath
```

3. Restart Claude Desktop and open Civil 3D. The **Horizun Hub** ribbon tab shows "Estado del puente", plus the two
   owner switches: **Canal C#** and **Escritura completa**. Both ask for confirmation and turn themselves off the
   next time Civil 3D starts.

Every installed file is checked against the package (SHA-256), and a failed install rolls back.

## Develop (Horizun developers)

Build targets include **Civil 3D 2024 and 2026**, with 2025/2027 retained. Use the
.NET 10 SDK and the actual Autodesk DLLs for the year/update being built. Core now
targets Framework 4.8, .NET 8 and .NET 10. Civil 3D 2026 changes runtime at 2026.2.2;
the installer inspects DLL metadata to select it. **Complete add-ins compile for
2024 and both 2026 runtimes against signed Autodesk references. Live validation
for those years remains pending.** See [COMPATIBILITY.md](docs/COMPATIBILITY.md).

- Branches: `develop` is where work happens; `main` only receives tested versions, and every version on `main` is
  tagged and published as a Release.
- `pwsh scripts/install.ps1 -RegisterClaudeDesktop` builds from source and installs the **development edition**. It
  adds a "Desarrollo" ribbon panel with **Sondeo API** and **Dibujo de ensayo** (the deterministic test drawing that
  `scripts/verify_live.py` checks against).
- `pwsh scripts/install.ps1 -Edition release -PackageOut horizun-civil3d-mcp- .zip` builds the **release
  edition** (no developer panel) as an installable zip for a GitHub Release.
- `-DryRun` builds and stages everything without installing anything.
- AI assistants: start with `CLAUDE.md` / `AGENTS.md` and `docs/handoff/00_START_HERE.md`. Personal working notes go
  in `.local/`, which git ignores.

## Surface tool

`horizun_c3d_surface` has 16 actions for reads, sampling, volumes, design comparison and confirmed, verified
surface edits. Live-verified on Civil 3D 2025 against the deterministic fixture (`HZ_BUILD_FIXTURE` +
`scripts/verify_live.py`): list, get, sample_elevation, volumes_report, compare_design, rename, duplicate_style,
set_style, create_tin, create_volume, rebuild, add_data and paste. `apply_elevation_analysis`,
`apply_slope_analysis` and `style_display` are built and unit-tested only (B + T) until their live gate runs.
The bridge does not undo writes (`undo_last` is disabled); use native Civil 3D UNDO. See
[surface operations](docs/SURFACES.md) and [the evidence matrix](docs/CIVIL3D.md).

## ChatGPT

ChatGPT can use this stdio server through OpenAI Secure MCP Tunnel. The installer includes isolated Civil 3D helpers; account setup and a real ChatGPT tool call complete the connection. See [ChatGPT setup and validation](docs/CHATGPT.md).

For an existing Civil 3D MCP installation, add only the helpers with `pwsh scripts/install-client-tools.ps1`; Civil 3D can remain open.

## Permission profiles

Profiles live in `%USERPROFILE%\.horizun\civil3d\settings.json`. Both the server and the plug-in read them.
They apply to **all Civil 3D instances of this Windows user**, as in Horizun Revit.
Selecting an instance does not isolate its permissions:

```json
{ "permission_profile": "safe_write", "allowed_tools": [], "denied_tools": [], "enable_execute_csharp": false, "paused": false }
```

| Profile | What it allows |
|---|---|
| `read_only` | Reading only |
| `safe_write` | Default. Typed drawing edits, each one undo group for native Civil 3D UNDO (the bridge does not undo them) |
| `full_write` | Also save, export and data shortcuts |
| `unsafe_code` | Also the C# escape hatch, together with `enable_execute_csharp` |

A settings file that cannot be parsed, or that names an unknown profile or an unknown tool in `allowed_tools` /
`denied_tools` (names are exact, e.g. `horizun_c3d_cleanup`), fails closed to `read_only`.

The C# escape hatch is arbitrary code, not a sandbox. `mode=query` aborts only
the supplied transaction; a script can still commit its own transaction or write
files. Typed drawing writes retain dry runs and post-commit verification.
